name: Celebrating mathematics for a better world 2021

content.title: Celebrating mathematics for a better world 2021
content.summary: AKU Tanzania marks this year's International Day of Mathematics

media.caption: Measurement of wood while making a teaching material during one of the teacher training workshops in Tanzania
media.alt: Celebrating mathematics for a better world 2021

content.text: "Mathematics is part and parcel of our daily life."

This is an observation made by Peter Kajoro, faculty from AKU's Institute for Educational Development, East Africa (IED,EA) following discussions on Facebook to celebrate this year's International Day of Mathematics. His role and those of other educators is to ensure that through effective teaching of the subject, attitudes are changed to view mathematics as something to be relied upon.

As part of the celebrations, IED EA in collaboration with the School of Nursing and Midwifery, East Africa (SONAM EA) and the Medical College, East Africa hosted a webinar to reflect on the importance of mathematics and improving the subject's teaching and learning. The webinar drew over 53participants from Tanzania , Kenya and Uganda which wrapped up pre-event discussions on Facebook.

SONAM EA faculty Dr Tumbwene Mwansisya who teaches bio-statistics to nurses, stressed the importance of mathematics in all fields and how its use can lead to good decision-making for example in the health sector. He emphasized the importance of helping learners appreciate the real-life application of mathematics.
"We cannot escape mathematics as it does not exclude anybody. It is a practical subject and we should embrace it," he said.

A similar view was expressed by Dr Mukasa Mohamed, a first-year resident who from the pre-event discussions highlighted the common theme that "mathematics is not just a classroom subject, it is something that we move with and work with even beyond the classroom".

Dr. Mukasa said that he has a great love for mathematics and attributed this fact to his primary teacher who told him "you need to juggle mathematics the way you juggle football." Linking the teaching and learning to mathematics to what learners like, will make the subject enjoyable and relatable.

Zaituni Ali, an alumna of IED, EA and a mathematics teacher pointed out teachers have the responsibility to teach through adopting pedagogy that will promote critical thinking which will facilitate learners to have the ability to think critically and solve problems in real-life situations.
Participants raised concerns such as how to ensure that mathematics is liked and not feared, the role of language and addressing the tension between different stakeholders of mathematics.

A clear message from the panelists was that none of these challenges were impossible but all required cooperation and collaboration first and foremost between teachers and students but also bringing on board other stakeholders especially parents. It was recommended that future event discussions on how such collaborations can be improved . Veronica Sarungi, faculty at IED, EA and moderator of the panel concluded by saying "Mathematics is for a better world and everyone should continue to reflect on how to make mathematics long-lasting in everybody's life."
